D012-D005_h001.question:

Once, during a routine check-up, I bolted from the exam room before the nurse could take my blood pressure. It’s embarrassing.

I only go to doctors now if my wife comes with me. If she’s there, holding my hand, talking me through it, I can usually sit still. I know it sounds irrational, but without her? I just can’t. It’s not that I think the needle’s going to do something… crazy… like inject poison or read my thoughts or anything. It’s just—I feel like my body’s going to shut down. I’ve never had delusions, never heard voices. But sometimes I wonder—am I losing control? Is this stress? A sign of something cracking inside? I don’t feel psychotic, but I can’t explain why a little blood hits me like a freight train.

If I see one— even a small one on a leash—my heart races, my hands get shaky, and I just need to get away, fast. It doesn’t matter if the dog looks friendly; I can’t trust myself to stay calm.
